connection_and_adoption_ownership: Successful application connections retain real OS lease/admission/backend owners. Unsafe callers must retain live paired connections and exclusive typed storage through synchronous invocation; final close follows the last invocation.

The adoption provider rejects null/equal/different-OS connections, invalid geometry and mismatched registered callback triples; it allocates the genuine additional lease/admission Box before the callback. The typed backend transfer nulls BOTH lease fields before seal/VMA effects. Untaken intact ownership may be released; partial/unknown transfer retains the real owner and returns EPROTO.

The MCCTRL adoption callback is a one-shot synchronous stack context backed by live parent/child Arcs. It validates geometry/child/MM/response/nonce proof and private registration state before paired-row reservation and irreversible MM publication. The backend retains sealed ingress owners/pins and does not reconstruct ownership from scalar claims.
independent_material_findings.consumer_selection: The actual selected .mcctrl_rust.o.cmd registers the adoption check-cfg but does not enable mckernel_current_fork_adoption_opt_in. Default MCCTRL has the genuine fork_control_current_v1 undefined import and no adopt_current_v4 relocation. Adoption remains source-declared/default-off; an exported symbol is not proof that its opt-in runtime path ran.
fork_control_capsule_ownership: The current MCCTRL route selects an already-owned unique child row, validates paired parent/slot/generation/PID and exact kernel request/worker/delivery identity, and supplies a real Box holding child/mirror Arcs plus a live DeferredModule pin. Scalar carrier values only select the existing owned row.

OwnedRevoke::take clears owner and all three callback fields before revoke/effects. Provider-owned ingress retains the capsule through the monotonic revoke/ACK phases; callbacks run outside the slots lock. Unknown/partial handoff and uncertain progress retain ownership. Only the authenticated destructor-ACK route permits acceptance, row release and release_after_ack.

The synchronous fork-control provider keeps both successful connections live, validates version/size and initial child field, supplies its actual backend child context and clears that transient field on return. The host releases only a wholly intact negative-return capsule; partial/unknown transfer has no fabricated rollback owner.
